name: Orbit AI - Phase 1 - Lead intake to Demo Dashboard

nodes.name: Lead intake webhook
nodes.notes: Fire-and-forget: acknowledges immediately rather than waiting on location resolution + both parallel research calls + the CRM writes to finish, since the caller (website form / scraper handoff / manual add) doesn't need that result synchronously.

nodes.name: Normalize lead fields
nodes.notes: UNCONFIRMED field shape - assumes the lead-intake caller posts these exact field names. Per CRM-OBJECT-MODEL.md (object model migration): gbpUrl added as its own field, separate from websiteUrl - Location is explicitly GBP-driven, so it's the primary key used to search/create the Location record, with websiteUrl as a fallback. Still assumes the Opportunity itself already exists (opportunityId supplied) - this workflow resolves/creates its Location, not the Opportunity. tcpaConsent is new this pass (05 Section 1: 'TCPA consent capture - recorded at entry; no consent = excluded from auto-dial') - coerced to a real boolean (`=== true`) rather than trusting whatever truthy/falsy value the caller sends, so a missing or malformed field defaults to false (no consent), never silently true.

nodes.name: Search Location by GBP/website
nodes.notes: NEW (object model migration, CRM-OBJECT-MODEL.md): Location is a real object as of this pass, not folded into Opportunity fields. Searches by gbpUrl first, falling back to websiteUrl if no GBP link was provided - same priority order the input cascade (checkpoint 3 of the KB generator) already uses elsewhere in this repo. UNVERIFIED: the filter query syntax, same Twenty CRM REST-shape caveat as every workflow in this library.

nodes.name: Location exists?
nodes.notes: UNVERIFIED: assumes a list response wraps records under 'data' or 'results' - tries both rather than committing to one guess, same pattern used elsewhere in this library (e.g. get-opportunity.mts).

nodes.name: Create Location

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ name: $('Normalize lead fields').item.json.companyName, gbpUrl: $('Normalize lead fields').item.json.gbpUrl, websiteUrl: $('Normalize lead fields').item.json.websiteUrl, opportunityId: $('Normalize lead fields').item.json.opportunityId, contractStatus: 'None' }) }}

nodes.notes: contractStatus starts 'None' per CRM-OBJECT-MODEL.md - this is the field Location Contract Lock will check once that enforcement workflow is built (Step 2/3, not this pass). Same Twenty CRM REST-shape uncertainty as every workflow here.

nodes.name: Location resolved
nodes.notes: Convergence point for the two IF branches above (only one runs per execution) - re-emits a single consistently-named locationId so every downstream node can reference $('Location resolved').item.json.locationId regardless of which branch actually produced it, rather than trying to conditionally reference two different upstream node names.

nodes.name: Deep Dive Research
nodes.notes: Deep Dive Research doesn't exist as a built service yet - see this node's notes in earlier versions of this file for the full caveat. Now runs AFTER Location resolution rather than immediately off Normalize (a deliberate simplification from the previous 3-way-parallel-fan-out design - avoids needing a second uncertain Merge node; the added latency of resolving Location first is a reasonable tradeoff, not a correctness issue, since DDR doesn't need locationId as an input anyway). Still runs in PARALLEL with Front Door Audit, per the Launch Checklist's explicit requirement - both branch off 'Location resolved.'

nodes.name: Front Door Audit

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ websiteUrl: $('Normalize lead fields').item.json.websiteUrl, companyName: $('Normalize lead fields').item.json.companyName, locationId: $('Location resolved').item.json.locationId }) }}

nodes.notes: Still a named placeholder service (10 audit categories not specified - see workflows/README.md). Now includes locationId in the request, since the audit result is about to be written onto that Location record, not the Opportunity - Front Door Audit is inherently per-site per CRM-OBJECT-MODEL.md.

nodes.name: Merge research + audit
nodes.notes: UNVERIFIED: same Merge-node parameter-shape caveat as before - the single most likely node in this workflow to need hand-fixing on import.

nodes.name: Write Front Door Audit to Location

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ frontDoorAuditStatus: 'Complete', frontDoorAuditScore: $('Front Door Audit').item.json.score, frontDoorAuditReportUrl: $('Front Door Audit').item.json.reportUrl }) }}

nodes.notes: MOVED from the Opportunity write (previous version of this workflow) to the Location, per CRM-OBJECT-MODEL.md: audits are per-site, and an Opportunity can span multiple Locations each needing their own independent audit result - writing this to the Opportunity would silently break the moment a second Location exists on the same deal. Still follows the Opportunity Card 'status + link, not raw content' principle.

nodes.name: Write Opportunity (stage: Demo Queue)

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ stage: 'Demo Queue', dueDiligenceStatus: 'Complete', dueDiligenceReportUrl: $('Deep Dive Research').item.json.reportUrl, locationIds: [$('Location resolved').item.json.locationId], tcpaConsent: $('Normalize lead fields').item.json.tcpaConsent }) }}

nodes.notes: Deep Dive Research stays Opportunity-level (business-identity-level, not site-level) per CRM-OBJECT-MODEL.md. locationIds is set to a single-element array here, not appended - this workflow assumes it's the FIRST Location resolved for a freshly-created Opportunity; a lead that already has other Locations attached would need a read-modify-write instead of this overwrite. Flagged, not silently wrong: worth revisiting once a real multi-location intake scenario exists to design against. Same Twenty CRM REST-shape uncertainty as every workflow here, and same Opportunity Card UX principle (status + links, not raw content).

main.node: Write Front Door Audit to Location
